title: Anupam Kher Mourns Jeffrey Archer, Recalls Priceless Dubai Literature Festival Meeting
excerpt: The veteran actor shared a photograph from their meeting at the Emirates Literature Festival in Dubai, where he presented Archer with his debut book. Archer, the author of Kane and Abel, died aged 86 on October 5 — a day before the release of his final novel.
body:
• Veteran actor Anupam Kher posted a social media tribute to British novelist Jeffrey Archer, who died on October 5, 2026, at the age of 86.
  • Kher recalled meeting Archer at the Emirates Literature Festival in Dubai, where he presented the author with his first book, The Best Thing About You Is You.
  • "A writer whose books I had held with such admiration was now holding mine," Kher wrote of their shared photograph.
  • Archer's final novel, Adam and Eve, released on October 6 — a day after his death. His publisher, HarperCollins, said he died "suddenly and peacefully" at home.

Veteran actor Anupam Kher has mourned the death of British novelist Jeffrey Archer, sharing a photograph from their meeting at the Emirates Literature Festival in Dubai and calling it "one of the highlights" of his life. Archer, whose novels Kane and Abel and Not a Penny More, Not a Penny Less made him one of the world's bestselling authors, died on October 5 at the age of 86, his publisher HarperCollins announced.

In a note posted on social media, the 71-year-old actor recalled presenting Archer with his own first book, The Best Thing About You Is You, at the Dubai festival. "Deeply saddened by the passing of the great storyteller, #JeffreyArcher. I have been, and will always remain, a great admirer of his writing," Kher wrote, adding that Archer's books "showed his extraordinary ability to draw readers into a world they never wanted to leave."

Context & Background

Kher's meeting with Archer took place when the actor travelled to Dubai for the Emirates Literature Festival shortly after launching his debut book. Archer, who had watched the Oscar-nominated Silver Linings Playbook, instantly recognized Kher — who played Dr. Patel in the film — and the two spoke about Indian cinema and Indian food, according to reports from the time. Archer liked the title of Kher's book, signed it for him and asked him to keep in touch.

https://x.com/AnupamPKher/status/2107690584689324383

The encounter stayed with Kher long after. He asked the author what he considered the most important thing for a writer. "We had a lovely chat," Kher recalled. "What stayed with me from his answer was 'the importance of memory' and 'imagination.' Those words have remained with me ever since."

Impact & Analysis

Archer's death was announced on Monday by HarperCollins, which said he died "suddenly and peacefully" at home between writing sessions — on the eve of publication of what he had said would be his final novel, Adam and Eve, released on October 6. A day earlier, he had appeared at a sold-out event at London's Leicester Square Theatre alongside broadcaster Gyles Brandreth, and he had been due to discuss the book at the Cheltenham Literature Festival. He is survived by his wife, Dame Mary Archer, their two sons, two granddaughters and three grandsons.

Across a five-decade career, Archer sold more than 300 million books in 119 countries and 49 languages, writing more than 30 novels including the Clifton Chronicles. His life supplied its own plot twists: elected a Conservative MP at 29 and a senior party official under Margaret Thatcher in the 1980s, he was convicted of perjury in 2001 and served two years in prison, where he wrote A Prison Diary. Tributes have poured in from across the world — Queen Camilla called him an "irrepressible life force," while HarperCollins chief executive Kate Elton described him as "the master storyteller and an editor's dream."

"I was an actor and a first-time author, but beside him, I was simply an excited admirer."

— Anupam Kher

Diaspora Angle

For millions of Indian readers, Archer was a fixture of growing up — his novels sat on bookshelves and in railway-station bookstalls across the country. Kher's tribute also underlines Dubai's role as a cultural crossroads for the diaspora: the Emirates Literature Festival has become a regular meeting point where South Asian and Western cultural figures cross paths. That their encounter was sparked by a Hollywood film — Archer recognized Kher from Silver Linings Playbook — says something about how freely Bollywood, Hollywood and the literary world now circulate among a globally mobile Indian audience.

What's Next / Looking Ahead

Adam and Eve, Archer's final novel, is now in bookstores, closing a writing career that began with his 1976 debut. Readers who never met the author will encounter him one last time through it — much as Kher returned to his own encounter through an old photograph. "Thank you, Mr. Archer, for your stories, your warmth, and for holding my first book with such kindness," Kher wrote. "It is a memory I will always cherish."
